'''Gustave Joseph Frerotte''' ({{IPAc-en|f|ə|ˈ|r|ɒ|t}}; born July 31, 1971) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Washington Redskins]] in the seventh round of the [[1994 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1994 National Football League Draft {{!}} Pro Football Hall of Fame |url=https://www.profootballhof.com/news/2005/01/news-1994-national-football-league-draft |access-date=November 12, 2023 |website=pfhof |language=en |archive-date=November 12, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231112030918/https://www.profootballhof.com/news/2005/01/news-1994-national-football-league-draft |url-status=live }}</ref>  He played [[college football]] at [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane football|Tulsa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FrerGu00.htm|title=Gus Frerotte|publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.Com|access-date=December 21, 2012|archive-date=January 10, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130110101809/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FrerGu00.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

Frerotte was selected to the [[1997 Pro Bowl]] while with the Redskins.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Justice |first=Richard |date=January 26, 1997 |title=FREROTTE HEADED FOR PRO BOWL |language=en-US |newspaper=Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1997/01/26/frerotte-headed-for-pro-bowl/50b5ea07-2ba9-4904-9c52-b46ca10b057d/ |access-date=November 12, 2023 |issn=0190-8286 |archive-date=August 28, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170828224403/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1997/01/26/frerotte-headed-for-pro-bowl/50b5ea07-2ba9-4904-9c52-b46ca10b057d/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He also played for the [[Detroit Lions]], [[Denver Broncos]], [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[Miami Dolphins]], [[Minnesota Vikings]], and [[St. Louis Rams]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gus Frerotte Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FrerGu00.htm |access-date=November 12, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121201510/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FrerGu00.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Gregory Raleigh Bingham''' (born March 13, 1951) is a former [[National Football League]] (NFL) [[linebacker]], who played from 1973 through 1984 for the [[Houston Oilers]]. He had 4 touchdowns and led the league in tackles for 11 years.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.chron.com/sports/texans/article/concussions-and-the-nfl-gregg-bingham-1704480.php | title=Concussions and the NFL: Gregg Bingham | date=October 24, 2010 }}</ref> He played football at [[Chicago]]'s [[DePaul College Prep|Gordon Tech High School]] as a tight end and linebacker and was the team's leading tackler.

Bingham went on from Gordon Tech to play middle guard / nose tackle for the [[Purdue Boilermakers]], starting 1971 through 1973, his last three years.  Known for "going all out on every single play", Bingham earned first-team All-[[Big Ten]] honors in his junior and senior years of 1971 and 1972 and likely would have in 1970 his sophomore year if not for breaking his ankle in an early season upset of then-ranked #3 [[Stanford University]] in [[Palo Alto]].

Bingham is a noted [[coin collector]] and has owned an extensive collection of [[Early United States commemorative coins|commemorative half dollars]],<ref>{{cite web|title=NGC Certifies Bingham Collection of U.S. Commemoratives|url=http://www.ngccoin.com/news/viewarticle.aspx?NewsletterNewsArticleID=328|publisher=[[Numismatic Guaranty Corporation]]|accessdate=28 April 2015}}</ref> as well as a complete collection of [[Morgan dollar]]s.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Ganz|first1=David L.|title=Insider's Report|url=http://www.numismedia.com/insider/00-12.shtml|accessdate=28 April 2015}}</ref>

Prior to the NFL, Skrepenak had starred as a [[college football]] player in the [[Big Ten Conference]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]]. He was a two-time [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]], team [[Captain (sports)|captain]], and four-year starter from [[1988 NCAA Division I-A football season|1988]]-[[1991 NCAA Division I-A football season|1991]].<ref name=Bentley>{{cite web|url=https://bentley.umich.edu/athdept/football/fballam/aaskrepe.htm|title=Greg Skrepenak|access-date=2007-10-28|publisher=The Regents of the University of Michigan|date=2007-02-10|work=University of Michigan Athletics History}}</ref> Skrepenak played on four consecutive Big Ten champion teams, appeared in three [[Rose Bowl (game)|Rose Bowl]]s and won a Gator Bowl [[Most valuable player|MVP]]. Previously he had been a scholar athlete at [[G. A. R. Memorial Junior Senior High School]] where he earned 12 [[varsity letter]]s in football, [[basketball]] and [[baseball]].<ref name=CGAS>{{cite web|url=http://www.luzernecounty.org/county/commissioners/gregory_a_skrepenak|access-date=2007-10-28|date=2006-09-01|title=Commissioner Gregory A. Skrepenak|publisher=Luzerne County |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071014204244/http://www.luzernecounty.org/county/commissioners/gregory_a_skrepenak |archive-date = October 14, 2007}}</ref>
